validated_results.title: Dietary vitamin C, E, and carotenoid intake and risk of renal cell carcinoma.
authors: Canadian Cancer Registries Epidemiology Research Group
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study of dietary vitamin C intake and incident, histologically confirmed renal cell carcinoma; no quantitative estimate for vitamin C reported in the abstract, only a narrative null finding.

extraction.population: Incident histologically confirmed RCC cases and population controls in 8 Canadian provinces

sample_size.excerpt: Between 1994 and 1997 in 8 Canadian provinces, mailed questionnaires were completed by 1,138 incident, histologically confirmed cases of RCC and 5,039 population controls, including information on socio-economic status, lifestyle habits and diet.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 1138 + 5039 = 6177

cases.excerpt: Between 1994 and 1997 in 8 Canadian provinces, mailed questionnaires were completed by 1,138 incident, histologically confirmed cases of RCC and 5,039 population controls, including information on socio-economic status, lifestyle habits and diet.

design.excerpt: Odds ratios (OR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were computed using unconditional logistic regression.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: A 69-item food frequency questionnaire provided data on eating habits 2 years before data collection.

gender.excerpt: The significant inverse association with beta-carotene and lutein/zeaxanthin was more pronounced in women
